name: Mark Zuckerberg

summary.text: Mark Zuckerberg is the founder and chief executive of Meta Platforms (formerly Facebook). He testified before a joint hearing of the Senate Judiciary and Commerce Committees on April 10, 2018 about the Cambridge Analytica episode, saying 'It was my mistake, and I'm sorry.' The FTC's July 2019 order requires him to certify quarterly that Facebook's privacy program complies with the order, and bars Facebook officers, including him, from the board's Independent Privacy Committee. In May 2022 the D.C. Attorney General sued him personally over the episode.

facts.claim: Zuckerberg was the sole witness at the April 10, 2018 joint Senate Judiciary and Commerce hearing 'Facebook, Social Media Privacy, and the Use and Abuse of Data'. His written testimony said about 300,000 people installed the app that gathered data, with access extending to tens of millions of their friends, and acknowledged Facebook's failures: 'It was my mistake, and I'm sorry.'
facts.quote: It was my mistake, and I'm sorry.

facts.claim: At the hearing Zuckerberg said Facebook's mantra was now 'move fast with stable infrastructure' and framed the core failure as not taking a broad enough view of the company's responsibility; he later answered written questions for the record from the Commerce Committee on the user agreement, non-user tracking and ad targeting.

facts.claim: Under the FTC's July 2019 order, Zuckerberg must certify quarterly, under threat of civil and criminal penalties, that Facebook's privacy program complies with the order; the FTC's majority statement said some commissioners argued the order was ineffective because it did not remove all of Zuckerberg's power over the board.
facts.quote: certifying quarterly, under threat of civil and criminal penalties, that the company's privacy program is in compliance with the Order

facts.claim: The 2019 FTC order disqualifies Facebook officers and employees, including Zuckerberg, from the board's Independent Privacy Committee.
facts.quote: Facebook officers and employees, including Mr. Zuckerberg, are disqualified from membership.

sources.title: Fact Sheet on 2019 FTC Order with Facebook

facts.claim: In May 2022 District of Columbia Attorney General Karl Racine sued Zuckerberg personally under the District's Consumer Protection Procedures Act, alleging he and Facebook knowingly gave third parties such as Cambridge Analytica access to the data of millions of users including 340,000 D.C. residents; a judge had earlier rejected an attempt to add him as a defendant in the District's existing suit against Facebook. This is an allegation.
facts.quote: Facebook and Zuckerberg knowingly gave third-party companies like Cambridge Analytica access to the information of millions, including 340,000 Washington D.C. residents
